sources.name: Public Health England
sources.text: "PHE statement on delayed reporting of COVID-19 cases" (published 4 Oct 2020, updated 5 Oct 2020), Michael Brodie, Interim Chief Executive: 15,841 cases between 25 September and 2 October not included in reported daily cases; 11,968, over 75%, due between 30 September and 2 October; identified overnight on Friday 2 October; transferred to contact tracing by 1am on 3 October; files that "exceeded the maximum file size" in the data load process; the mitigation that "splits large files"; everyone affected received their result as normal. The statement does not use the words Excel, XLS, rows or columns.

sources.name: Hansard, House of Commons
sources.text: "Covid-19 Update", 5 October 2020, vol 681: the Health Secretary's 15,841 over the previous 8 days; "a failure in the automated transfer of files"; "a PHE legacy system"; the July decision to replace it and contracts "awarded in August"; "a maximum file size error"; 6,500 hours of extra contact tracing; 51% contacted a second time as of 9am; "This incident should never have happened". Questions from 2 opposition MPs, Jonathan Ashworth (Leicester South) and Neil Coyle (Bermondsey and Old Southwark), are the only places "Excel" appears in the debate record.

sources.name: Science and Technology Committee
sources.text: Letter from Rt Hon Greg Clark MP, Chair, to Baroness Dido Harding, 8 October 2020: the statement that the Secretary of State told the House the legacy system "included the use of Microsoft Excel"; "It is reported that PHE developers used an old format of the software, XLS"; the question on certification of "the Microsoft Excel-based system".

sources.name: Baroness Harding, National Institute for Health Protection
sources.text: Reply to Greg Clark, 12 October 2020: "The technical issue was not caused by the use of an old format"; Excel files that "exceeded their file size threshold and so were not uploaded" as Pillar 2 volumes rose; the 24 September to 1 October date range; 6,000 hours of extra contact tracing; "(75% / 11,968)"; the 79% reach figure as of 12 October, quoted as written; "A full wash-up of the incident is ongoing".

sources.name: Department of Health and Social Care
sources.text: "Weekly statistics for NHS Test and Trace (England) and coronavirus testing (UK): 1 October to 7 October" (updated 22 Oct 2020): 15,841 cases identified between 25 September and 2 October. Supports the ledger's first row; no separate reach rate for the delayed cases is published.

sources.name: Office for Statistics Regulation
sources.text: "Now, about that Excel spreadsheet..." (blog, 15 Oct 2020): the error "was not directly part of official statistics production"; the review of reproducible analytical pipelines. Gives no figures.

sources.name: UK Health Security Agency
sources.text: "COVID-19 Archive data download" (last updated 1 May 2025), the archive of the decommissioned Coronavirus (COVID-19) in the UK dashboard: the chart's 2 series, England (E92000001), from Cases/nation_newCasesByPublishDate.csv and Cases/nation_newCasesBySpecimenDate.csv in cases.zip (downloaded 10 Oct 2026); "Data presented by 'publish date' is not a reliable indicator of trends over time since this represents the date on which data was first published and may include the publication of a backlog of data or subsequent revisions to the data"; "It has not been possible to fully validate these archived datasets against the latest version of the decommissioned Coronavirus (COVID-19) in the UK dashboard."
